sampling_model.design: Known fixed \(r=2\) Conflict Graph Design using the formal direct-effect conflict graph \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\), generated from independent desired-exposure coordinates in Perron-priority rank order.
sampling_model.units: One triangular array of \(n\) fixed labeled units with fixed graph and fixed potential outcomes; there is no super-population sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: The only randomness is \(U_{n,i}\), and Algorithm 1 maps it to the realized binary assignment \(Z_n\).
sampling_model.overlap: The endpoint exposure probability is known exactly as \(q_{n,i}=(4\lambda_n)^{-1}t_n^{|B_{n,i}|}\); for edgeless \(G_n\), \(\lambda_n=1\), \(B_{n,i}=\varnothing\), and \(q_{n,i}=1/4\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no statistical nuisance functions; \(\lambda_n\), \(q_{n,i}\), and \(\mathbf V_n\) are design-computable.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.6 proves asymptotic normality when the maximum conflict degree is \(o(n^{1/9})\).
Proposition 5.8 constructs a direct-effect sequence whose standardized CGD estimator does not converge in distribution.
Propositions 5.3 and 5.4 establish additive and ratio consistency, respectively, for the spectral variance-bound estimator.
Corollary 5.7 gives conservative Wald coverage under the paper's sufficient CLT regime.

Theorem 2.3 gives a Kolmogorov bound for dependency-graph sums with finite \(L^{\delta}\) moments for \(\delta\in[3,\infty)\); the direct fourth-moment substitution here sets \(\delta=4\). Theorem 2.1 is the bounded-summand result, and Theorem 2.4 treats \(\delta\in(2,3)\), so neither is the direct comparison for this class.
The discrete-time theorem bounds martingale normal approximation using increment moments and normalized predictable quadratic variation.
The paper characterizes admissible estimable conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs.
The preprint derives design-based upper and lower bounds on minimax mean-squared point-estimation risk in terms of local and global conflict-graph connectivity.

tldr: For the fixed \(r=2\) component-Perron Conflict Graph Design estimator, the sharp worst-case uniform normal-inference frontier is \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), with no additional slowly varying boundary factor. The proved quantitative bound is \(C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\{D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)+D_n/n\}^{1/5}\); repeated Perron-ordered stars give a legal non-normal convolution obstruction at the critical scale. The observable spectral variance-bound estimator is uniformly ratio-consistent in the normal regime and yields conservative feasible Wald coverage. In addition, the graph-adaptive condition \(D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)\to0\) is a sufficient pointwise rule for all three conclusions. Only the exact interior Kolmogorov rate, matched legal lower arrays for its vanishing terms, and optimized constants remain open.

project_justification.gap: The published CGD theorem proves normality only under \(d_{\max}=o(n^{1/9})\), while its nonconvergence example does not identify the intervening worst-case degree frontier; generic dependency-graph bounds also discard the ordered prefix structure used by the fixed design.
project_justification.niche: The independent desired-exposure coordinates admit an exact forward Doob decomposition, and componentwise Perron priority controls both fourth moments of the increments and fluctuations of their predictable quadratic variation without imposing a maximum-outcome bound.
project_justification.fill: The proved martingale bound yields the quantitative error \(C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\{D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)+D_n/n\}^{1/5}\), repeated stars certify failure at every fixed \(n^{2/3}\) scale, and together they establish the necessary-and-sufficient maximum-degree criterion \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\). The same analysis proves spectral-bound ratio consistency and conservative feasible Wald coverage, while the graph-adaptive rule \(D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)\to0\) supplies a sufficient refinement for individual graph sequences.

related_work: \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} supplies the fixed \(r=2\) design, estimator, spectral variance bound, the \(o(n^{1/9})\) sufficient CLT in Theorem 5.6, the direct-effect nonconvergence construction in Proposition 5.8, additive and ratio consistency in Propositions 5.3--5.4, and the Wald result in Corollary 5.7. Its formal direct-effect conflict graph has operator \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\); Appendix D.9 writes the star value as \(\sqrt{n-1}\) by suppressing the formal loop contribution, whereas the exact loop-inclusive value is \(1+\sqrt{n-1}\). The present fixed-\(B,c\), direct-effect, component-Perron specialization strictly strengthens the published sufficient distributional and coverage regimes. \cite{HeydeBrown1970DepartureNormality} supplies the fourth-moment martingale normal-approximation theorem used in the proof; \cite{Haeusler1988MartingaleRate}, \cite{Bolthausen1982ExactMartingaleRates}, and \cite{Mourrat2013MartingaleRate} explain the role of predictable-quadratic-variation fluctuations and the unresolved exact-rate question. Theorem 2.3 of \cite{JanischLehericy2024SparseDependencyGraph}, specialized to \(\delta=4\), is the direct generic dependency-graph comparison, but it does not exploit CGD prefix products. \cite{Ross2011FundamentalsStein}, \cite{Chin2019SteinInterference}, and \cite{CaiShaoZhang2026RefinedLocalDependence} are supporting local-dependence comparisons rather than probability theorems claimed to be sharpened here. \cite{KandirosHarshawSavje2026MinimaxNetwork} optimizes designs and estimators for minimax mean-squared point-estimation risk, a different target from the fixed-CGD Kolmogorov frontier. \cite{AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference} supplies the exposure-weighted design-based baseline, and \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance} motivates estimating a conservative quadratic bound rather than the generally unidentified exact randomization variance. Declaration 18.13 of \cite{BlairCoppockHumphreys2023ResearchDesign}, modeled after \cite{GreenKrasnoCoppockFarrerLenoirZingher2016LawnSigns}, supplies the concrete \(238\)-precinct queen-adjacency direct-effect inquiry \(\operatorname{mean}(Y_{1,0}-Y_{0,0})\). The declaration itself uses Bernoulli assignment and Aronow--Samii estimation; the present theorem is an asymptotic design rule for future replications that instead adopt fixed CGD, not a retrospective validation of that analysis.
technical_internal_limitation: The proved \(1/5\)-power Kolmogorov bound is inherited from a general fourth-moment martingale inequality. The present argument establishes the exact convergence frontier but does not establish that this quantitative rate is constant-order sharp inside \(d=o(n^{2/3})\), nor does it optimize constants. The graph-adaptive condition \(D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)\to0\) is sufficient for an individual legal sequence and is not claimed necessary graph by graph. The variance result estimates the conservative spectral bound \(\mathrm{VB}_n\), which can strictly exceed \(\sigma_n^2\); it does not identify the exact variance.
honest_scope: The note fixes uniform constants \(B\) and \(c\), the finite-population direct effect, the fixed \(r=2\) CGD estimator, and componentwise Perron ordering. This is a legal fixed-design specialization using one of the anchor's permitted importance orderings, while \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\) is a fixed-constant finite-\(n\) uniformization rather than literally the anchor's full asymptotic Assumptions 1--5. The fourth-moment restrictions imply the corresponding second-moment restrictions by \(n^{-1}\sum_i a_{n,i}^2\le(n^{-1}\sum_i a_{n,i}^4)^{1/2}\le\sqrt B\), and similarly for \(b_{n,i}\). Under the uniform frontier, \(\lambda_n\le D_n\le d_n=o(n^{2/3})\) implies \(\lambda_n=o(n)\); under the graph-adaptive sufficient rule, \(\lambda_n/n\le D_n^2/(n\lambda_n)\to0\). The repeated-star witnesses also satisfy \(\lambda_n=1+\sqrt{k_n}=O(n^{1/3})=o(n)\). Conversely, whenever an anchor sequence has finite uniform endpoint fourth-moment bounds and \(\liminf_n n\sigma_n^2/\lambda_n>0\), fixed constants \(B\ge1\) and \(c\in(0,1]\) can be chosen so that the sequence is eventually in \(\mathcal M_n(D_n;B,c)\). The iff claim concerns the worst-case maximum-degree envelope \(K_n(d_n;B,c)\), not necessity for each individual graph sequence. Wald coverage is conservative because \(\mathrm{VB}_n\ge\sigma_n^2\), and no exact-coverage or exact-variance-estimation claim is made. The result is an asymptotic benchmark for future fixed-CGD replications; it does not provide a finite-\(n\) certificate for the \(238\)-precinct declaration or retroactively validate its Bernoulli assignment and Aronow--Samii intervals. The only remaining mathematical gap is the exact interior Kolmogorov rate, including legal lower arrays matching its vanishing terms and optimized constants.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Generic rank in the Perron-priority reveal order.

symbols.name: G_n
symbols.def: Known labeled interference relation on \(\mathcal I_n\); simplicity and undirectedness are imposed separately.

symbols.name: \mathcal H_n
symbols.def: Formal direct-effect conflict graph operator \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\), including one loop at each unit.

symbols.name: \pi_n
symbols.def: Unit-to-rank permutation: \(\pi_n(i)=1\) is the first reveal, and within each connected component of \(G_n\), smaller ranks correspond to larger positive unit-norm Perron coordinates of \(\mathcal H_n\), with label ties and components broken by the smallest label.

symbols.name: p_n
symbols.def: Probability \(p_n=(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\) that a desired-exposure coordinate is nonnull.

symbols.name: \mathbb P_U
symbols.def: Probability under the product law of \(U_{n,i}\), conditional on the fixed graph and potential outcomes.

symbols.name: Z_n
symbols.def: Assignment returned by Algorithm 1 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} with \(r=2\), formal direct-effect conflict graph \(\mathcal H_n\), rank map \(\pi_n\), and desired coordinates \(U_{n,i}\).

symbols.name: Y_{n,i}(\mathbf z)
symbols.def: Fixed potential outcome of unit \(i\) under assignment \(\mathbf z\).

symbols.name: \mathbf e_{n,i}
symbols.def: Assignment treating \(i\) and no other unit.

symbols.name: C_0
symbols.def: A universal finite positive constant large enough for the stated moment and ratio bounds.

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)
symbols.def: Finite constant depending only on \(B\) and \(c\).

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: Fixed tolerance for variance-bound ratio concentration.

symbols.name: d_{\mathrm K}
symbols.def: Kolmogorov distance \(d_{\mathrm K}(X,Z)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P(X\le x)-\mathbb P(Z\le x)|\).

symbols.name: \mathsf P_n
symbols.def: Matrix with \((\mathsf P_n)_{ji}=1\) exactly when \(j\in B_{n,i}\), so rows index earlier parents and columns index later children.

symbols.name: S_{n,i}
symbols.def: Independent Rademacher sign encoding labels \(1\) and \(0\) on the event \(R_{n,i}=1\).

symbols.name: \mathcal F_{n,s}
symbols.space: A filtration on the product assignment space.
symbols.def: Rank-indexed filtration \(\mathcal F_{n,0}=\{\varnothing,\Omega\}\) and \(\mathcal F_{n,s}=\sigma(U_{n,\rho_n(1)},\ldots,U_{n,\rho_n(s)})\) for \(1\le s\le n\).

symbols.name: M_{n,s}
symbols.def: Rank-\(s\) increment \(M_{n,s}=\mathbb E_U[F_n\mid\mathcal F_{n,s}]-\mathbb E_U[F_n\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]\).

symbols.name: \Delta_{n,s}Q_n
symbols.def: Signed coordinate difference of \(Q_n\) between setting \(R_{n,\rho_n(s)}=1\) and setting \(R_{n,\rho_n(s)}=0\), holding all other reveal coordinates fixed.

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm W}(B,c,\alpha)
symbols.def: Finite constant depending only on \(B\), \(c\), and \(\alpha\).

symbols.name: \mathcal R_n(d;B,c)
symbols.def: Exact order, up to constants, of \(K_n(d;B,c)\), to be derived by \(\mathrm{oeq:optimal\text{-}kolmogorov\text{-}rate}\).

assumptions.condition: \(G_n\) is a simple undirected graph on \(\mathcal I_n\).
\(Y_{n,i}(\mathbf z)=Y_{n,i}(\mathbf z')\) whenever \(z_j=z'_j\) for every \(j\in\{i\}\cup\mathcal N_{G_n}(i)\).

definitions.name: Perron priority order
definitions.construction: For each connected component of \(G_n\), take a positive unit-norm Perron eigenvector of the component block of \(\mathcal H_n\), assign ranks by decreasing coordinate with label ties, and concatenate components by their smallest label. This defines the unit-to-rank map \(\pi_n\), its inverse \(\rho_n=\pi_n^{-1}\), and \(B_{n,i}=\{j:\{i,j\}\in G_n,\ \pi_n(j)<\pi_n(i)\}\).

definitions.name: Independent desired-exposure law
definitions.construction: Independently for \(i\in\mathcal I_n\), draw \(U_{n,i}=1\) and \(U_{n,i}=0\) with probability \((4\lambda_n)^{-1}\) each and draw \(U_{n,i}=*\) with probability \(t_n=1-(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\); set \(E_{n,i,k}=\{U_{n,i}=k,\ U_{n,j}=*\text{ for all }j\in B_{n,i}\}\) and \(q_{n,i}=(4\lambda_n)^{-1}t_n^{|B_{n,i}|}\).

definitions.name: Fixed \(r=2\) Conflict Graph Design
definitions.construction: Apply Algorithm 1 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} with \(r=2\), formal direct-effect conflict graph \(\mathcal H_n\), rank map \(\pi_n\), and coordinates \(U_{n,i}\) to obtain \(Z_n\); the strict earlier-neighbor sets are \(B_{n,i}\) from \(G_n\). On \(E_{n,i,1}\) the algorithm realizes \(\mathbf e_{n,i}\) in unit \(i\)'s closed \(G_n\)-neighborhood, and on \(E_{n,i,0}\) it realizes \(\mathbf 0_n\) there.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)=\left\{(G_n,Y_n):\ G_n\text{ is simple and undirected},\ Y_n\text{ satisfies arbitrary neighborhood interference on }G_n,\ D_n\le d,\ \frac1n\sum_i|a_{n,i}|^4\le B,\ \frac1n\sum_i|b_{n,i}|^4\le B,\ \sigma_n^2\ge\frac{c\lambda_n}{n}\right\}.\]

definitions.name: Forward CGD Doob decomposition
definitions.construction: At reveal rank \(s\), let \(J_{n,s}=\sum_{i:(\mathsf P_n)_{\rho_n(s),i}=1}\delta_{n,i}h_{n,i,<s}\), \(C_{n,s}=\delta_{n,\rho_n(s)}h_{n,\rho_n(s)}/p_n-J_{n,s}/t_n\), and \(G_{n,s}=\gamma_{n,\rho_n(s)}h_{n,\rho_n(s)}/p_n\). The coordinate identity to audit is \[M_{n,s}=C_{n,s}(R_{n,\rho_n(s)}-p_n)+G_{n,s}R_{n,\rho_n(s)}S_{n,\rho_n(s)},\qquad Q_n=p_n\sum_{s=1}^n\{t_nC_{n,s}^2+G_{n,s}^2\}.\]

definitions.name: Critical repeated-star construction
definitions.construction: For fixed \(\beta>0\), take \(k_n=\lfloor\beta n^{2/3}\rfloor\), \(m_n=\lfloor n/(k_n+1)\rfloor\) disjoint stars with \(k_n\) leaves, and isolated padding vertices; put \(a_{n,i}=1,b_{n,i}=0\) on leaves and \(a_{n,i}=b_{n,i}=0\) elsewhere.

definitions.name: CGD Kolmogorov-rate handle
definitions.construction: Determine \(\mathcal R_n(d;B,c)\) by pairing the forward martingale moment terms from \(\mathrm{def:doob\text{-}decomposition}\) with lower bounds obtained from optimized legal block-star arrays and perturbations of their hub-trigger counts.

statements.statement: For every \((G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\), \(1\le\lambda_n\le D_n\), \(\lambda_n\ge\sqrt{D_n}\), \(|B_{n,i}|\le\lambda_n-1\), and the oriented matrix satisfies \(\|\mathsf P_n\|_{2\to2}\le\lambda_n\), \(\|\mathsf P_n\|_{4\to4}\le\sqrt{\lambda_nD_n}\), and \(\|\mathsf P_n^{\top}\|_{4\to4}\le\lambda_n\).
statements.justification: These inequalities translate Perron priority into the operator norms needed to avoid a squared dependency neighborhood.
statements.gap: \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} uses Perron order for design and variance control but not this \(\ell_4\) martingale chain.
statements.consumer: The prefix and operator bounds are the deterministic input to the uniform normal-approximation theorem.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a member of \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\), and write \(A=A_{G_n}\), \(\lambda=\lambda_n\), \(D=D_n\), and \(\mathsf P=\mathsf P_n\).  Since \(A\) is the adjacency matrix of a simple undirected graph by \(\mathrm{ass:simple\text{-}graph}\), for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
 x^{\mathsf T}Ax=2\sum_{\{i,j\}\in G_n}x_ix_j
 \le \sum_{i=1}^n\deg_{G_n}(i)x_i^2\le(D-1)\|x\|_2^2.
\]
The same calculation applied to \(|x|\), together with \(|x^{\mathsf T}Ax|\le |x|^{\mathsf T}A|x|\), shows that \(\|A\|_{2\to2}=\lambda_{\max}(A)=\lambda-1\).  Hence \(1\le\lambda\le D\).

If \(D>1\), choose a vertex \(v\) of degree \(D-1\), put \(x_v=2^{-1/2}\), put \(x_j=\{2(D-1)\}^{-1/2}\) for its neighbors, and put all other coordinates equal to zero.  Then \(\|x\|_2=1\), and the edges incident to \(v\), with all other edge contributions nonnegative, give
\[
 \lambda-1=\lambda_{\max}(A)\ge x^{\mathsf T}Ax\ge\sqrt{D-1}.
\]
For \(D=1\) the same conclusion is immediate.  Thus
\[
 \lambda\ge1+\sqrt{D-1}\ge\sqrt D.
\]

Consider a connected component \(C\), let \(x^C\) be the positive Perron vector used by \(\mathrm{def:perron\text{-}order}\), and let \(\lambda_C\) be the largest eigenvalue of \(I+A_C\).  If \(j\in B_{n,i}\), the ordering gives \(x^C_j\ge x^C_i>0\).  The Perron equation therefore gives
\[
 (\lambda_C-1)x^C_i=\sum_{j:\{i,j\}\in G_n}x^C_j
 \ge |B_{n,i}|x^C_i.
\]
Division is legal because \(x^C_i>0\), and \(\lambda_C\le\lambda\); hence \(|B_{n,i}|\le\lambda-1\).

Entrywise, \(|\mathsf Px|\le A|x|\), so \(\|\mathsf P\|_{2\to2}\le\lambda-1\le\lambda\).  A row of \(\mathsf P\) lists later neighbors of one unit and has at most \(D-1\) ones, while a row of \(\mathsf P^{\mathsf T}\) lists \(B_{n,i}\) and has at most \(\lambda-1\) ones.  To obtain the fourth-norm bounds without an interpolation hypothesis, let \(r_j\) be the row sum of a nonnegative zero-one matrix \(M\).  Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 |(Mx)_j|^2\le r_j\{M(|x|^2)\}_j,
\]
and consequently, if \(r_j\le r\),
\[
 \|Mx\|_4^4\le r^2\|M(|x|^2)\|_2^2
 \le r^2\|M\|_{2\to2}^2\|x\|_4^4.
\]
Apply this first with \(M=\mathsf P\), \(r=D\), and then with \(M=\mathsf P^{\mathsf T}\), \(r=\lambda\).  Since \(\|\mathsf P^{\mathsf T}\|_{2\to2}=\|\mathsf P\|_{2\to2}\le\lambda\), this yields
\[
 \|\mathsf P\|_{4\to4}\le\sqrt{\lambda D},\qquad
 \|\mathsf P^{\mathsf T}\|_{4\to4}\le\lambda,
\]
which proves every asserted inequality.

statements.statement: For the rank-indexed filtration in \(\mathrm{def:doob\text{-}decomposition}\), the displayed coordinate formula satisfies \(F_n-\mathbb E_UF_n=\sum_{s=1}^nM_{n,s}\), \(\mathbb E_U[M_{n,s}\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]=0\), and \(Q_n=\sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U[M_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]\), with \(\mathbb E_UQ_n=n^2\sigma_n^2\).
statements.justification: This proposed identity exposes the independent-coordinate filtration that the published unit-level dependency graph discards.
statements.gap: Algorithm 1 in \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} is sequential, but its published CLT does not derive these increments.
statements.consumer: An independently verified identity would permit direct use of quantitative martingale normal approximation.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(p=p_n\), \(t=t_n\), \(R_i=R_{n,i}\), \(S_i=S_{n,i}\), \(h_i=h_{n,i}\), and suppress \(n\) on the endpoint coefficients.  On \(E_{n,i,1}\) and \(E_{n,i,0}\), \(\mathrm{def:cgd\text{-}assignment}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:arbitrary\text{-}neighborhood\text{-}interference}\) imply that the observed outcome is respectively \(a_i\) and \(b_i\).  Since \(q_{n,i}=(p/2)t^{|B_{n,i}|}\), the elementary label identity
\[
 a_i\mathbf 1\{U_{n,i}=1\}-b_i\mathbf 1\{U_{n,i}=0\}
 =\frac{R_i}{2}(\delta_i+\gamma_iS_i)
\]
turns \(\mathrm{def:cgd\text{-}estimator}\) into the exact raw-sum identity
\[
 F_n=\sum_{i=1}^nh_i\frac{R_i}{p}(\delta_i+\gamma_iS_i).
\]
The factors in \(h_i\) involve only coordinates preceding \(i\), hence are independent of \((R_i,R_iS_i)\).  Moreover \(\mathbb E_Uh_i=1\), \(\mathbb E_UR_i=p\), and \(\mathbb E_U(R_iS_i)=0\).  It follows that
\[
 \mathbb E_UF_n=\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_i=n\tau_n.
\]

Put \(u=\rho_n(s)\).  The summand indexed by \(u\) has conditional expectation \(\delta_u h_u\) before rank \(s\), and its change after revealing \(U_{n,u}\) is
\[
 \frac{\delta_uh_u}{p}(R_u-p)+\frac{\gamma_uh_u}{p}R_uS_u.
\]
For a later unit \(i\) with \((\mathsf P_n)_{u i}=1\), all unrevealed factors have conditional mean one.  Its conditional expectation changes by
\[
 \delta_i h_{n,i,<s}\left\{\frac{1-R_u}{t}-1\right\}
 =-\frac{\delta_i h_{n,i,<s}}{t}(R_u-p).
\]
No other summand changes.  Summing these displayed changes gives exactly
\[
 M_{n,s}=C_{n,s}(R_{n,u}-p_n)+G_{n,s}R_{n,u}S_{n,u}.
\]
Every factor in \(C_{n,s}\) and \(G_{n,s}\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{n,s-1}\).  Conditional on that sigma-field, \(R_{n,u}\) is Bernoulli with success probability \(p_n\), the signed variable \(R_{n,u}S_{n,u}\) is centered, and their cross moment is zero.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_U[M_{n,s}\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]=0,\qquad
 \mathbb E_U[M_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]
 =p_n\{t_nC_{n,s}^2+G_{n,s}^2\}.
\]
The defining conditional expectations telescope, so \(F_n-\mathbb E_UF_n=\sum_sM_{n,s}\); summing the last display proves the stated formula for \(Q_n\).  Orthogonality of martingale differences then gives
\[
 \mathbb E_UQ_n=\sum_s\mathbb E_UM_{n,s}^2
 =\operatorname{Var}_U(F_n)=n^2\operatorname{Var}_U(T_n)=n^2\sigma_n^2.
\]

statements.statement: The candidate universal constant \(C_0<\infty\) can be chosen so that uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\), \[\sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U|M_{n,s}|^4\le C_0Bn\lambda_nD_n^2,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_U(Q_n)\le C_0Bn\lambda_n^2D_n.\] At every reveal rank \(s\), the Bernoulli coordinate flip is conjectured to obey \[|\Delta_{n,s}Q_n|\le64p_n[\mathsf P_n\operatorname{diag}(w_n)(\lambda_nv_n+\mathsf P_n^{\top}v_n)]_{\rho_n(s)}.\]
statements.justification: This is the answer-open early-kill lemma: D0 must prove or refute it for overlapping prefixes and arbitrary signed endpoints.
statements.gap: Neither \cite{Haeusler1988MartingaleRate} nor \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} supplies a CGD-specific graph-uniform predictable-variation bound.
statements.consumer: If established, it would supply the candidate \(n^{2/3}\) normal regime without imposing a maximum-outcome bound.
statements.proof_tex:
Use the abbreviations of the preceding proof and write \(w=w_n\), \(v=v_n\), and \(\mathsf P=\mathsf P_n\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:perron\text{-}prefix\text{-}operator}\), \(|B_{n,i}|\le\lambda_n-1\).  Since \(-\log(1-x)\le x/(1-x)\) for \(0\le x<1\),
\[
 -(|B_{n,i}|)\log t_n
 \le\frac{\lambda_n-1}{2\lambda_n-1}<\frac12,
\]
so every full or partial prefix product is between zero and \(e^{1/2}<2\).  Also \(p_n^{-1}=2\lambda_n\) and \(t_n^{-1}\le2\).  Consequently, at \(u=\rho_n(s)\),
\[
 |J_{n,s}|\le2(\mathsf Pw)_u,\qquad
 |C_{n,s}|\le4\{\lambda_nw_u+(\mathsf Pw)_u\}=4v_u,\qquad
 |G_{n,s}|\le4\lambda_nw_u\le4v_u.
\]
For a Bernoulli variable \(R\) of mean \(p_n\),
\[
 \mathbb E|R-p_n|^4=p_nt_n^4+t_np_n^4\le2p_n,\qquad
 \mathbb E|RS|^4=p_n.
\]
Using \(|x+y|^4\le8(|x|^4+|y|^4)\) conditionally in the exact increment formula therefore yields \(\mathbb E_U|M_{n,s}|^4\le C p_nv_u^4\) for a universal \(C\).  Moreover,
\[
 \sum_iw_i^4\le8\sum_i(|a_{n,i}|^4+|b_{n,i}|^4)\le16Bn.
\]
The fourth-norm bounds in \(\mathrm{lem:perron\text{-}prefix\text{-}operator}\), \(p_n=(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\), and \(\lambda_n\le D_n\) now give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U|M_{n,s}|^4
 &\le Cp_n\|\lambda_nw+\mathsf Pw\|_4^4\\
 &\le Cp_n\{\lambda_n^4+\lambda_n^2D_n^2\}\|w\|_4^4
 \le C Bn\lambda_nD_n^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]

It remains to audit the coordinate flip.  Relabel units temporarily in reveal order, so that \(\mathsf P_{ki}=1\) means that \(k\) is an earlier parent of \(i\).  If a prefix product contains coordinate \(k\), its difference between \(R_k=1\) and \(R_k=0\), with all other coordinates fixed, is at most two; otherwise its difference is zero.  Therefore, for every increment index \(j\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\Delta_k C_j|
 &\le4\left\{\lambda_nw_j\mathsf P_{kj}
       +\sum_i\mathsf P_{ki}w_i\mathsf P_{ji}\right\},\\
 |\Delta_k G_j|&\le4\lambda_nw_j\mathsf P_{kj}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The second sum is precisely the shared-child contribution: both \(k\) and \(j\) are parents of \(i\).  This derivation allows arbitrary signs because absolute values were taken before summation.

At both values of \(R_k\), the preceding bounds give \(|C_j|\le4v_j\) and \(|G_j|\le4v_j\).  Hence \(|x^2-y^2|\le(|x|+|y|)|x-y|\), the formula for \(Q_n\), and \(t_n\le1\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\Delta_kQ_n|
 &\le64p_n\left[\sum_j\mathsf P_{kj}w_j\lambda_nv_j
  +\sum_i\mathsf P_{ki}w_i\sum_j\mathsf P_{ji}v_j\right]\\
 &=64p_n[\mathsf P\operatorname{diag}(w)
       (\lambda_nv+\mathsf P^{\mathsf T}v)]_k.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus the displayed conjectured envelope is valid, including for overlapping parent prefixes.

For completeness, variance tensorization here follows directly from the coordinate-reveal martingale of the function \(Q_n(R_1,\ldots,R_n)\): conditional Jensen's inequality bounds the squared rank-\(k\) increment by \(p_nt_n\mathbb E[(\Delta_kQ_n)^2\mid R_1,\ldots,R_{k-1}]\).  Orthogonality and summation yield
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_U(Q_n)\le p_nt_n\sum_k\mathbb E_U(\Delta_kQ_n)^2
 \le4096p_n^3\|\mathsf P\operatorname{diag}(w)
 (\lambda_nv+\mathsf P^{\mathsf T}v)\|_2^2.
\]
For any vector \(x\), Holder's inequality and the already proved operator bounds give
\[
 \|\mathsf P\operatorname{diag}(w)x\|_2
 \le\lambda_n\|w\|_4\|x\|_4.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\lambda_nv+\mathsf P^{\mathsf T}v\|_4&\le2\lambda_n\|v\|_4,\\
 \|v\|_4&\le(\lambda_n+\sqrt{\lambda_nD_n})\|w\|_4
 \le2\sqrt{\lambda_nD_n}\|w\|_4.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Combining the last three displays, substituting \(p_n=(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\), and using \(\|w\|_4^4\le16Bn\), gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_U(Q_n)\le C Bn\lambda_n^2D_n.
\]
Enlarging one universal constant proves all three claims with the stated \(C_0\).

statements.statement: For each fixed \(B\ge1\) and \(0<c\le1\), the constant \(C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)<\infty\) may be chosen so that every member of \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\) satisfies \[d_{\mathrm K}((T_n-\tau_n)/\sigma_n,Z_0)\le\min\left\{1,C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\left(\frac{D_n^2}{n\lambda_n}+\frac{D_n}{n}\right)^{1/5}\right\}\le\min\left\{1,C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\left(\frac{2D_n^{3/2}}n\right)^{1/5}\right\}.\] Consequently \(K_n(d;B,c)\le\min\{1,C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)(2d^{3/2}/n)^{1/5}\}\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \((G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\), and put
\[
 s_n^2=n^2\sigma_n^2.
\]
Membership in \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\), specifically \(\mathrm{ass:variance\text{-}floor}\), gives
\[
 s_n^2\ge c n\lambda_n>0,
\]
because \(c>0\), \(n\ge1\), and \(\lambda_n\ge1\).  Thus division by \(s_n\) is legal.  The exposure realization in \(\mathrm{def:cgd\text{-}assignment}\), arbitrary neighborhood interference, and \(q_{n,i}=\mathbb P_U(E_{n,i,k})>0\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_UF_n
 &=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_n}\mathbb E_U\left[
 a_{n,i}\frac{\mathbf 1(E_{n,i,1})}{q_{n,i}}
 -b_{n,i}\frac{\mathbf 1(E_{n,i,0})}{q_{n,i}}
 \right]\\
 &=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_n}(a_{n,i}-b_{n,i})
 =n\tau_n.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This proves, rather than defines, the equality between the expectation of the observed-data estimator and the fixed causal contrast.

By \(\mathrm{lem:exact\text{-}forward\text{-}doob}\), the variables
\[
 X_{n,s}=M_{n,s}/s_n,\qquad 1\le s\le n,
\]
form a martingale-difference sequence relative to \((\mathcal F_{n,s})_{s=0}^n\), and
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_UX_{n,s}^2
 =\frac{\mathbb E_UQ_n}{s_n^2}=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U[X_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]
 =\frac{Q_n}{s_n^2}.
\]
The fourth moments are finite by \(\mathrm{lem:prefix\text{-}flip\text{-}moments}\).  Hence the cited Heyde--Brown inequality \(\mathrm{lem:heyde\text{-}brown\text{-}martingale\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment}\) applies and yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_{\mathrm K}\left(\frac{F_n-\mathbb E_UF_n}{s_n},Z_0\right)
 &\le C\left\{
 \frac{\sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U|M_{n,s}|^4}{s_n^4}
 +\mathbb E_U\left|\frac{Q_n}{s_n^2}-1\right|^2
 \right\}^{1/5}\\
 &=C\left\{
 \frac{\sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U|M_{n,s}|^4}{s_n^4}
 +\frac{\operatorname{Var}_U(Q_n)}{s_n^4}
 \right\}^{1/5}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The equality uses \(\mathbb E_UQ_n=s_n^2\), again from \(\mathrm{lem:exact\text{-}forward\text{-}doob}\).  Applying the two inequalities in \(\mathrm{lem:prefix\text{-}flip\text{-}moments}\) and the lower bound \(s_n^4\ge c^2n^2\lambda_n^2\) gives, term by term,
\[
 \frac{\sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U|M_{n,s}|^4}{s_n^4}
 \le \frac{C_0B D_n^2}{c^2n\lambda_n},
 \qquad
 \frac{\operatorname{Var}_U(Q_n)}{s_n^4}
 \le \frac{C_0B D_n}{c^2n}.
\]
Since \(F_n=nT_n\), \(\mathbb E_UF_n=n\tau_n\), and \(s_n=n\sigma_n\), the standardized variable on the left is exactly \((T_n-\tau_n)/\sigma_n\).  Absorbing \(C\), \(C_0\), \(B\), and \(c^{-2}\) into \(C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\), and using that Kolmogorov distance is at most one, proves
\[
 d_{\mathrm K}\left(\frac{T_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n},Z_0\right)
 \le \min\left\{1,C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)
 \left(\frac{D_n^2}{n\lambda_n}+\frac{D_n}{n}\right)^{1/5}\right\}.
\]

By \(\mathrm{lem:perron\text{-}prefix\text{-}operator}\), \(\lambda_n\ge\sqrt{D_n}\); and \(D_n\ge1\).  Therefore
\[
 \frac{D_n^2}{n\lambda_n}\le\frac{D_n^{3/2}}n,
 \qquad
 \frac{D_n}{n}\le\frac{D_n^{3/2}}n.
\]
Adding these two inequalities gives the sum at most \(2D_n^{3/2}/n\), proving the second pointwise bound with the same displayed constant \(C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)\).  Finally, \(D_n\le d\) for every member of \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\).  Taking the two suprema in \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}error}\) therefore gives
\[
 K_n(d;B,c)\le\min\left\{1,C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)
 \left(\frac{2d^{3/2}}n\right)^{1/5}\right\},
\]
as claimed.
statements.justification: The theorem gives the proved graph-sensitive Kolmogorov bound from primitive fourth-moment, variance-floor, and Perron-prefix conditions.
statements.gap: Theorem 5.6 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} requires \(d=o(n^{1/9})\); direct substitution of Theorem 2.3 of \cite{JanischLehericy2024SparseDependencyGraph} at \(\delta=4\) does not attain the CGD-specific bound.
statements.consumer: Future fixed-CGD replications can check either the worst-case degree rule or the graph-adaptive sufficient rule before using a normal critical value.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\beta>0\), the construction in \(\mathrm{def:repeated\text{-}star\text{-}witness}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_n(k_n+1;B,c)\) eventually for every fixed \(B\ge1\) and \(0<c\le1\), has \(D_n/n^{2/3}\to\beta\), and satisfies \[(T_n-\tau_n)/\sigma_n\Rightarrow\mathcal L_{\beta}=\mathcal L\left(\sqrt{8/9}Z_0-\frac{N_{r_{\beta}}-r_{\beta}}{3\sqrt{r_{\beta}}}\right).\] The law \(\mathcal L_{\beta}\) has variance one and nonzero third cumulant \(-1/(27\sqrt{r_{\beta}})\), so it is not \(\mathcal N(0,1)\).
statements.justification: This conjectural critical compound limit is the proposed legal obstruction under the original fourth moments and variance floor.
statements.gap: Proposition 5.8 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} alternates a single star with another graph and does not locate the worst-case degree boundary.
statements.consumer: If independently proved, the construction would supply necessity for degree envelopes that are not \(o(n^{2/3})\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\beta>0\), and abbreviate \(k=k_n\), \(m=m_n\).  Eventually \(k\ge2\) and \(m\ge1\).  On every star, the positive Perron coordinate of the hub is \(\sqrt{k}\) times a leaf coordinate, so \(\mathrm{def:perron\text{-}order}\) places the hub before all leaves.  The graph has
\[
 D_n=k+1,\qquad \lambda_n=1+\sqrt{k}.
\]
Choose the full potential-outcome schedule \(Y_{n,i}(\mathbf z)=z_i\) on leaves and zero on hubs and padding vertices.  It depends only on a unit's own treatment and therefore satisfies \(\mathrm{ass:arbitrary\text{-}neighborhood\text{-}interference}\).  Its endpoints are exactly those in \(\mathrm{def:repeated\text{-}star\text{-}witness}\), and
\[
 \frac1n\sum_i|a_{n,i}|^4=\frac{mk}{n}\le1\le B,\qquad
 \frac1n\sum_i|b_{n,i}|^4=0.
\]

Put \(p=(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\), \(t=1-p\), and \(\eta=p/2=(4\lambda_n)^{-1}\).  For star \(\ell\), let \(Q_\ell^\star\) indicate that its hub is null and let \(N_\ell\) count leaves whose desired label is one.  Independence of the desired coordinates gives
\[
 Q_\ell^\star\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(t),\qquad
 N_\ell\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\eta),
\]
with mutual independence within and across stars.  Only leaves contribute to \(F_n=nT_n\), and the exact contribution of star \(\ell\) is
\[
 F_\ell=\frac{Q_\ell^\star N_\ell}{t\eta}.
\]
Thus \(\mathbb E_UF_\ell=k\), and direct evaluation of its second moment gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_U(F_\ell)
 =\frac{k(1-\eta)}{\eta t}+\frac{k^2p}{t}.
\]
Writing \(s_n^2=n^2\sigma_n^2=m\operatorname{Var}_U(F_\ell)\), the relations
\[
 k\sim\beta n^{2/3},\quad m\sim n/k,\quad
 p\sim(2\sqrt{k})^{-1},\quad\eta\sim(4\sqrt{k})^{-1},\quad t\to1
\]
imply
\[
 s_n^2\sim\frac92n\sqrt{k},\qquad
 \frac{s_n^2}{n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow\frac92.
\]
Consequently \(\sigma_n^2\ge c\lambda_n/n\) eventually for every \(0<c\le1\).  This proves eventual membership in \(\mathcal M_n(k_n+1;B,c)\), and \(D_n/n^{2/3}\to\beta\).

Define
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 A_n&=\sum_{\ell=1}^m\frac{N_\ell-k\eta}{\eta},\\
 B_n&=k\sum_{\ell=1}^m\left(\frac{Q_\ell^\star}{t}-1\right),\\
 C_n&=\sum_{\ell=1}^m\left(\frac{Q_\ell^\star}{t}-1\right)
              \frac{N_\ell-k\eta}{\eta}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Expanding the product proves the exact decomposition
\[
 F_n-\mathbb E_UF_n=A_n+B_n+C_n.
\]
The first two terms are independent.  The factors in each summand of \(C_n\) are independent and centered, so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_U(C_n)
 =m\frac pt\frac{k(1-\eta)}\eta=O(n),\qquad
 \mathbb E_U(C_n/s_n)^2=O(k^{-1/2})\longrightarrow0.
\]

The variable \(A_n\) is a sum of \(mk\) independent centered Bernoulli terms divided by \(\eta\), with variance \(mk(1-\eta)/\eta\).  The sum of their fourth moments divided by the squared variance is \(O((mk\eta)^{-1})\), and
\[
 mk\eta\sim\frac{n}{4\sqrt{k}}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Its predictable quadratic variation is deterministic.  The cited fourth-moment martingale bound \(\mathrm{lem:heyde\text{-}brown\text{-}martingale\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment}\) therefore proves a normal limit after standardization.  Since
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{Var}_U(A_n)}{s_n^2}\longrightarrow\frac89,
\]
we have \(A_n/s_n\Rightarrow\sqrt{8/9}\,Z_0\).

Let \(H_n=\sum_{\ell=1}^m(1-Q_\ell^\star)\).  Then \(H_n\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,p)\),
\[
 mp\longrightarrow r_\beta=\frac1{2\beta^{3/2}},\qquad
 B_n=-\frac{k}{t}(H_n-mp),\qquad
 \frac{k}{ts_n}\longrightarrow\frac1{3\sqrt{r_\beta}}.
\]
For every fixed nonnegative integer \(q\), the binomial mass formula gives
\[
 \mathbb P_U(H_n=q)=\binom mq p^q(1-p)^{m-q}\longrightarrow
 e^{-r_\beta}\frac{r_\beta^q}{q!}.
\]
The laws are uniformly tight because \(\sup_n\mathbb E_UH_n<\infty\).  Independence of \(A_n\) and \(H_n\), truncation to finitely many values of \(H_n\), and the preceding pointwise mass limits now give
\[
 \frac{A_n+B_n}{s_n}\Rightarrow
 \sqrt{8/9}\,Z_0-\frac{N_{r_\beta}-r_\beta}{3\sqrt{r_\beta}},
\]
with the two limiting variables independent.  Since \(C_n/s_n\to0\) in probability, the same weak limit holds for \((F_n-\mathbb E_UF_n)/s_n=(T_n-\tau_n)/\sigma_n\).

The Gaussian summand has variance \(8/9\), while the centered scaled Poisson summand has variance \(1/9\); hence the limit has variance one.  Cumulants add for independent variables, and the third cumulant of a Poisson variable of intensity \(r_\beta\) is \(r_\beta\).  Therefore the third cumulant of the displayed limit is
\[
 -\frac{r_\beta}{27r_\beta^{3/2}}=-\frac1{27\sqrt{r_\beta}}\ne0.
\]
A standard normal variable has third cumulant zero, so the limit is not standard normal.  Its convolution with the nondegenerate Gaussian component has a continuous density, completing the proof.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(B\ge1\), every fixed \(0<c\le1\), and every integer sequence \(1\le d_n\le n\), \[K_n(d_n;B,c)\longrightarrow0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_n=o(n^{2/3}).\] No additional slowly varying boundary factor is present.
statements.proof_tex:
Suppose first that \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}normal\text{-}bound}\),
\[
 K_n(d_n;B,c)\le C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)
 \left(\frac{2d_n^{3/2}}n\right)^{1/5}\longrightarrow0.
\]

Conversely, suppose \(d_n\) is not \(o(n^{2/3})\).  There are \(\epsilon>0\) and a subsequence, still denoted by \(n\), on which \(d_n\ge\epsilon n^{2/3}\).  Fix \(0<\beta<\epsilon\), and use \(\mathrm{def:repeated\text{-}star\text{-}witness}\) with \(k_n=\lfloor\beta n^{2/3}\rfloor\).  Then \(k_n+1\le d_n\) eventually on this subsequence, and \(\mathrm{thm:repeated\text{-}star\text{-}boundary}\) supplies a member of \(\mathcal M_n(d_n;B,c)\) whose standardized estimator converges weakly to \(\mathcal L_\beta\).

Let \(F_\beta\) be the distribution function of \(\mathcal L_\beta\).  It is continuous because the law has a Gaussian component.  Pointwise convergence of distribution functions to a continuous distribution function is uniform: choose finite tail cutoffs and a finite grid on which the increments of \(F_\beta\) are small, and use monotonicity between adjacent grid points.  Therefore, along the chosen subsequence,
\[
 d_{\mathrm K}\left(\frac{T_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n},Z_0\right)
 \longrightarrow \sup_z|F_\beta(z)-\Phi(z)|=:\delta_\beta.
\]
The last quantity is strictly positive because \(\mathrm{thm:repeated\text{-}star\text{-}boundary}\) proves \(\mathcal L_\beta\ne\mathcal N(0,1)\).  Since \(K_n(d_n;B,c)\) is a supremum over a class containing this witness, it cannot converge to zero.  This proves the equivalence.  The same critical power appears on both sides with arbitrary fixed \(\beta>0\), so no extra slowly varying boundary factor is present.
statements.justification: This candidate iff statement is the field-tier target, contingent on D0 verification of both the martingale upper bound and the repeated-star limit.
statements.gap: No cited paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient degree condition for the fixed \(r=2\) CGD estimator; \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} gives only \(1/9\) sufficiency and a nonsharp obstruction.
statements.consumer: A verified frontier would supply a single asymptotic design rule for deciding when CGD normal inference is uniformly justified.

statements.statement: The universal constant \(C_0<\infty\) may be chosen so that every \((G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\) satisfies \[L_n\le C_0\lambda_n,\qquad n^2\sigma_n^2\le L_nH_{2,n},\qquad \mathbb E_U\widehat H_{2,n}=H_{2,n},\qquad \operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat H_{2,n})\le2C_0Bn\lambda_n.\]
statements.justification: This proposed squared-endpoint reduction would turn the published CGD operator inequality into uniform moment control for the observable scale.
statements.gap: Propositions 5.3--5.4 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} establish additive and ratio consistency for the spectral variance-bound estimator, respectively, but not this fixed-class quantitative package.
statements.consumer: The inequalities supply the denominator and numerator controls for uniform ratio consistency.
statements.proof_tex:
For arbitrary deterministic real arrays \(x=(x_i)\) and \(y=(y_i)\), define
\[
 F_n(x,y)=\sum_i\left\{x_i\frac{\mathbf1(E_{n,i,1})}{q_{n,i}}
 -y_i\frac{\mathbf1(E_{n,i,0})}{q_{n,i}}\right\}.
\]
The exact decomposition proved in \(\mathrm{lem:exact\text{-}forward\text{-}doob}\) applies algebraically with endpoints \(x_i,y_i\).  Put \(w_i=|x_i|+|y_i|\) and \(v=\lambda_nw+\mathsf P_nw\).  The pointwise coefficient bounds in the proof of \(\mathrm{lem:prefix\text{-}flip\text{-}moments}\) give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_U\{F_n(x,y)\}=\mathbb E_UQ_n(x,y)
 \le32p_n\|v\|_2^2.
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:perron\text{-}prefix\text{-}operator}\),
\[
 \|v\|_2\le2\lambda_n\|w\|_2,\qquad
 \|w\|_2^2\le2\sum_i(x_i^2+y_i^2).
\]
Since \(p_n=(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\), enlargement of the universal constant gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_U\{F_n(x,y)\}
 \le C_0\lambda_n\sum_i(x_i^2+y_i^2).
\]

If \(\theta=(x_i,y_i)_{i=1}^n\), then the sign convention \(s_1=1,s_0=-1\) gives \(F_n(x,y)=\theta^{\mathsf T}W_n\), and hence
\[
 \theta^{\mathsf T}\mathbf V_n\theta\le C_0\lambda_n\|\theta\|_2^2
\]
for every \(\theta\in\mathbb R^{2n}\).  The Rayleigh-quotient characterization of the largest eigenvalue of the symmetric positive semidefinite matrix \(\mathbf V_n\) yields \(L_n\le C_0\lambda_n\).

For the actual endpoints, \(F_n=nT_n\) and its coefficient vector has squared norm \(H_{2,n}\).  Therefore
\[
 n^2\sigma_n^2=\operatorname{Var}_U(F_n)
 \le L_nH_{2,n}.
\]
Endpoint realization on \(E_{n,i,k}\) gives
\[
 \widehat H_{2,n}=F_n((a_{n,i}^2)_i,(-b_{n,i}^2)_i).
\]
The expectation identity from the same Horvitz--Thompson algebra is thus
\[
 \mathbb E_U\widehat H_{2,n}=\sum_i\{a_{n,i}^2-(-b_{n,i}^2)\}=H_{2,n}.
\]
Applying the just-proved variance inequality to these transformed endpoints and then using the two fourth-moment assumptions gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_U(\widehat H_{2,n})
 \le C_0\lambda_n\sum_i(a_{n,i}^4+b_{n,i}^4)
 \le2C_0Bn\lambda_n.
\]
One common enlargement of \(C_0\) proves the lemma.

statements.statement: The universal constant \(C_0<\infty\) may be chosen so that every \((G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\) obeys \(\mathrm{VB}_n\ge\sigma_n^2>0\) and, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\mathbb P_U\left(\left|\frac{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}{\mathrm{VB}_n}-1\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le\frac{C_0B\lambda_n}{c^2n\varepsilon^2}.\] Consequently the class supremum is at most \(C_0Bd/(c^2n\varepsilon^2)\), so the ratio converges to one uniformly whenever \(d_n=o(n)\), including the sharp normal regime.
statements.justification: This expanded-regime ratio statement is a candidate downstream consequence and is not treated as established before D0 verification.
statements.gap: Propositions 5.3--5.4 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} establish additive and ratio consistency, respectively, while \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance} explains why exact variance cannot replace this bound.
statements.consumer: If proved, it would make the candidate normal frontier usable with observed outcomes rather than the inaccessible exact variance.
statements.proof_tex:
The variance floor implies \(\sigma_n^2>0\).  By \(\mathrm{lem:spectral\text{-}bound\text{-}moments}\),
\[
 \mathrm{VB}_n=\frac{L_nH_{2,n}}{n^2}\ge\sigma_n^2>0.
\]
In particular both \(L_n\) and \(H_{2,n}\) are positive, and the same lemma plus \(\mathrm{ass:variance\text{-}floor}\) gives
\[
 H_{2,n}\ge\frac{n^2\sigma_n^2}{C_0\lambda_n}\ge\frac{cn}{C_0}.
\]
Division by \(\mathrm{VB}_n\) is therefore legal, and \(\mathrm{def:spectral\text{-}bound}\) gives
\[
 \frac{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}{\mathrm{VB}_n}
 =\frac{\widehat H_{2,n}}{H_{2,n}}.
\]
Chebyshev's inequality and the variance bound in \(\mathrm{lem:spectral\text{-}bound\text{-}moments}\) now imply, after enlarging \(C_0\),
\[
 \mathbb P_U\left(\left|\frac{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}{\mathrm{VB}_n}-1\right|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le\frac{2C_0Bn\lambda_n}{\varepsilon^2(cn/C_0)^2}
 \le\frac{C_0B\lambda_n}{c^2n\varepsilon^2}.
\]
Since \(\lambda_n\le D_n\le d\), taking the class supremum replaces \(\lambda_n\) by \(d\).  For \(d=d_n=o(n)\) the resulting bound tends to zero for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), uniformly over the class.  The regime \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\) is a subset of this ratio-consistency regime.

statements.statement: For each fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the constant \(C_{\mathrm W}(B,c,\alpha)<\infty\) may be chosen so that \[\inf_{(G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)}\mathbb P_U(\tau_n\in C_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha-2K_n(d;B,c)-C_{\mathrm W}(B,c,\alpha)(d/n)^{1/3}.\] Hence, if \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), then \(\liminf_n\inf_{\mathcal M_n(d_n;B,c)}\mathbb P_U(\tau_n\in C_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<\alpha<1\), put \(z=z_{1-\alpha/2}\), and let \(0<\varepsilon\le1\).  Define
\[
 \mathcal A_{n,\varepsilon}=
 \left\{\left|\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n/\mathrm{VB}_n-1\right|\le\varepsilon\right\}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{thm:spectral\text{-}ratio}\), \(\mathrm{VB}_n\ge\sigma_n^2>0\).  On \(\mathcal A_{n,\varepsilon}\), whenever \(\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n>0\),
\[
 \frac{z\sqrt{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}}{\sigma_n}
 \ge z\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}.
\]
When \(\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n=0\), \(\mathrm{def:wald\text{-}interval}\) returns \(\mathbb R\) and coverage is automatic.  Hence, writing \(X_n=(T_n-\tau_n)/\sigma_n\),
\[
 \mathbb P_U(\tau_n\notin C_{n,\alpha})
 \le\mathbb P_U\{|X_n|>z\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\}
 +\mathbb P_U(\mathcal A_{n,\varepsilon}^{\mathsf c}).
\]
The definition of \(K_n(d;B,c)\), applied separately to the two tails, gives
\[
 \mathbb P_U\{|X_n|>x\}\le2\{1-\Phi(x)\}+2K_n(d;B,c).
\]
Also, \(1-\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and the standard-normal density is at most \((2\pi)^{-1/2}\), so
\[
 2\{\Phi(z)-\Phi(z\sqrt{1-\varepsilon})\}
 \le\frac{2z}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\varepsilon.
\]
Since \(2\{1-\Phi(z)\}=\alpha\), \(\mathrm{thm:spectral\text{-}ratio}\) and \(\lambda_n\le d\) yield uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\),
\[
 \mathbb P_U(\tau_n\notin C_{n,\alpha})
 \le\alpha+2K_n(d;B,c)+C_\alpha\varepsilon
 +\frac{C_0Bd}{c^2n\varepsilon^2}.
\]
Choose \(\varepsilon=(d/n)^{1/3}\), which lies in \((0,1]\) because \(1\le d\le n\).  Absorbing the displayed constants into \(C_{\mathrm W}(B,c,\alpha)\) and taking the infimum of coverage probabilities proves the finite-error inequality.  If \(d_n=o(n^{2/3})\), then \(\mathrm{thm:sharp\text{-}degree\text{-}frontier}\), whose sufficiency now carries the explicit harmless factor \(2^{1/5}\), gives \(K_n(d_n;B,c)\to0\), while \((d_n/n)^{1/3}\to0\); the asserted uniform lower limit follows.
statements.justification: This expanded-regime coverage statement is a candidate downstream consequence of the unverified normal and ratio bounds.
statements.gap: Corollary 5.7 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} covers only its \(o(n^{1/9})\) pointwise regime.
statements.consumer: If proved, it would provide the CGD calibration rule for the concrete direct-effect inquiry in Declaration 18.13.

statements.statement: If \(G_n\) is edgeless, then \(D_n=\lambda_n=1\), every \(B_{n,i}=\varnothing\), and \(q_{n,i}=1/4\). The fixed \(r=2\) CGD estimator is therefore a sum of independent modified Horvitz--Thompson endpoint contrasts, and \(K_n(1;B,c)\to0\), recovering the classical independent triangular-array central limit theorem under the stated fourth moments and variance floor.
statements.proof_tex:
If \(G_n\) is edgeless, every degree is zero, so \(D_n=1\), \(A_{G_n}=0\), and \(\lambda_n=1\).  The definition of earlier neighbors gives \(B_{n,i}=\varnothing\), and \(\mathrm{def:desired\text{-}coordinate\text{-}design}\) gives \(q_{n,i}=1/4\).  Thus the centered raw estimator is the sum of the independent centered variables
\[
 X_{n,i}=4\{a_{n,i}\mathbf1(U_{n,i}=1)-b_{n,i}\mathbf1(U_{n,i}=0)\}-(a_{n,i}-b_{n,i}).
\]
Their aggregate fourth moment is bounded by \(CBn\), whereas the variance floor gives \(\operatorname{Var}_U(\sum_iX_{n,i})=n^2\sigma_n^2\ge cn\); this is the usual uniform Lyapunov condition.  Equivalently, substituting \(D_n=\lambda_n=1\) into \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}normal\text{-}bound}\) gives
\[
 K_n(1;B,c)\le C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)(2/n)^{1/5}\longrightarrow0.
\]
This is precisely the corrected degree envelope at \(D_n=1\), with the factor \(2\) retained inside the fifth root.  It proves the stated independent-design reduction and its central limit conclusion.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check at the no-interference boundary.
statements.gap: This is a consistency check against classical Berry--Esseen theory rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It verifies that the frontier does not distort ordinary independent randomization inference.

statements.statement: Conditional on D0 validating the candidate frontier, what is the exact order \(\mathcal R_n(d;B,c)\), up to constants depending only on \(B\) and \(c\), of \(K_n(d;B,c)\) throughout the resulting Gaussian regime; in particular, can legal CGD graph-and-endpoint arrays match each dominant verified martingale error term?
statements.justification: This secondary question is conditional: the degree frontier and its internal rate bound must first survive the answer-open D0 audit.
statements.gap: Exactness in \cite{Haeusler1988MartingaleRate} ranges over general martingales, and optimality in \cite{JanischLehericy2024SparseDependencyGraph} ranges over general dependency graphs; neither proves attainability by CGD arrays.
statements.consumer: A matched rate would quantify how conservative the asymptotic degree rule is at the finite graph sizes used in experiment planning.

obligation.what_is_open: The exact constant-order expression for \(\mathcal R_n(d;B,c)\) when \(d=o(n^{2/3})\), including a legal CGD lower array matching each dominant normal-approximation term.
obligation.obstruction: The verified Heyde--Brown bound has the generic martingale exponent \(1/5\), but its known sharpness examples are not shown to be representable by the constrained CGD prefix-product increments.  The repeated-star family proves a non-Gaussian critical boundary but does not match the vanishing \(1/5\)-power upper rate in the subcritical regime.
obligation.attempted: The forward Doob decomposition, the shared-parent flip envelope, the spectral operator chain, and the repeated-star hub-count perturbation were all derived.  They close the convergence frontier, but no CGD endpoint and graph array obtained from these constructions matches the generic martingale rate throughout the interior regime.
obligation.partial_result:
The verified results give the uniform upper bound
\[
 K_n(d;B,c)\le \min\left\{1,C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)
 \left(d^{3/2}/n\right)^{1/5}\right\}
\]
throughout the Gaussian regime \(d=o(n^{2/3})\).  At every fixed critical scale \(d_n\ge \beta n^{2/3}+o(n^{2/3})\), the repeated-star construction gives
\[
 \liminf_nK_n(d_n;B,c)\ge
 d_{\mathrm K}(\mathcal L_\beta,\mathcal N(0,1))>0.
\]
These conclusions determine the sharp convergence frontier but do not determine the exact vanishing order inside that frontier.

statements.statement:
Let \((X_s,\mathcal G_s)_{s=1}^N\) be a finite real martingale-difference sequence such that \(\sum_{s=1}^N\mathbb E X_s^2=1\) and \(\mathbb E|X_s|^4<\infty\).  There is a universal finite constant \(C\) such that, with \(S_N=\sum_{s=1}^N X_s\) and \(\langle S\rangle_N=\sum_{s=1}^N\mathbb E[X_s^2\mid\mathcal G_{s-1}]\),
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\left|\mathbb P(S_N\le x)-\Phi(x)\right|
 \le C\left\{\sum_{s=1}^N\mathbb E|X_s|^4+
 \mathbb E|\langle S\rangle_N-1|^2\right\}^{1/5}.
\]

source.locator: Theorem 1 specialized to fourth moments; standardized notation is reproduced in Fan and Shao (2018), Introduction, equations (2)--(3)
source.verbatim_statement: Define N_n = sum_{i=1}^n E|X_i|^{2p} + E|<S>_n-1|^p. When p in (1,2], Heyde and Brown proved that there exists a constant C_p depending only on p such that sup_{x in R}|P(S_n <= x)-Phi(x)| <= C_p N_n^{1/(2p+1)}.

statements.statement:
For fixed \(B\ge1\), \(0<c\le1\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), let \(((G_n,Y_n))_{n\ge1}\) be any sequence such that \((G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(D_n;B,c)\) for every \(n\).  The graph-adaptive condition
\[
 \frac{D_n^2}{n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow0
\]
is sufficient for
\[
 d_{\mathrm K}\left(\frac{T_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n},Z_0\right)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}{\mathrm{VB}_n}
 \xrightarrow{\mathbb P_U}1,
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P_U(\tau_n\in C_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha.
\]
For the repeated-star construction at any fixed \(\beta>0\), the same diagnostic converges instead to \(\beta^{3/2}>0\), while the standardized estimator converges to \(\mathcal L_{\beta}\ne\mathcal N(0,1)\).  Thus the repeated-star family is a nonvanishing-diagnostic elbow illustration; the sufficient condition is not asserted to be necessary for each individual graph sequence.
statements.proof_tex:
Set
\[
 r_n=\frac{D_n^2}{n\lambda_n},
 \qquad
 \kappa_n=d_{\mathrm K}\left(\frac{T_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n},Z_0\right).
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem:perron\text{-}prefix\text{-}operator}\), \(1\le\lambda_n\le D_n\).  Consequently
\[
 \frac{D_n}{n}=r_n\frac{\lambda_n}{D_n}\le r_n,
 \qquad
 \frac{\lambda_n}{n}=r_n\left(\frac{\lambda_n}{D_n}\right)^2\le r_n.
\]
If \(r_n\to0\), the unchanged graph-sensitive envelope in \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}normal\text{-}bound}\), applied pointwise to the member of \(\mathcal M_n(D_n;B,c)\), gives
\[
 \kappa_n\le C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)(2r_n)^{1/5}\longrightarrow0.
\]
This proves the normal limit directly from the primitive design bounds rather than assuming it.

For every fixed \(\eta>0\), \(\mathrm{thm:spectral\text{-}ratio}\) and the second displayed inequality give
\[
 \mathbb P_U\left(
 \left|\frac{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}{\mathrm{VB}_n}-1\right|>\eta
 \right)
 \le\frac{C_0B\lambda_n}{c^2n\eta^2}
 \le\frac{C_0B r_n}{c^2\eta^2}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Hence \(\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n/\mathrm{VB}_n\xrightarrow{\mathbb P_U}1\).  Notice also that \(\mathrm{thm:spectral\text{-}ratio}\) gives \(\mathrm{VB}_n\ge\sigma_n^2>0\), so all ratios used here are well defined.

It remains to prove feasible coverage using the actual error \(\kappa_n\), rather than a worst-case envelope indexed only by \(D_n\).  Put \(z=z_{1-\alpha/2}>0\),
\[
 u_n=\frac{\lambda_n}{n},
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_n=u_n^{1/3},
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_n=\left\{
 \left|\frac{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}{\mathrm{VB}_n}-1\right|
 \le\varepsilon_n\right\}.
\]
We have \(0<u_n\le1\), because \(1\le\lambda_n\le D_n\le n\), and \(u_n\le r_n\to0\).  Thus eventually \(0<\varepsilon_n<1\).  On \(\mathcal A_n\),
\[
 \widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n
 \ge(1-\varepsilon_n)\mathrm{VB}_n
 \ge(1-\varepsilon_n)\sigma_n^2.
\]
If \(\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n=0\), \(\mathrm{def:wald\text{-}interval}\) returns \(\mathbb R\), so noncoverage is impossible.  Otherwise, with \(X_n=(T_n-\tau_n)/\sigma_n\), the preceding inequality implies
\[
 \mathbb P_U(\tau_n\notin C_{n,\alpha})
 \le \mathbb P_U\{|X_n|>z\sqrt{1-\varepsilon_n}\}
 +\mathbb P_U(\mathcal A_n^{\mathsf c}).
\]
The definition of \(\kappa_n\), applied to the two tails, yields
\[
 \mathbb P_U\{|X_n|>x\}\le2\{1-\Phi(x)\}+2\kappa_n
 \quad(x\ge0).
\]
Because \(2\{1-\Phi(z)\}=\alpha\), the standard normal density is bounded by \((2\pi)^{-1/2}\), and \(1-\sqrt{1-\varepsilon_n}\le\varepsilon_n\), it follows that
\[
 2\{1-\Phi(z\sqrt{1-\varepsilon_n})\}
 \le\alpha+\frac{2z}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\varepsilon_n.
\]
Finally, \(\mathrm{thm:spectral\text{-}ratio}\) with \(\eta=\varepsilon_n\) gives
\[
 \mathbb P_U(\mathcal A_n^{\mathsf c})
 \le\frac{C_0B u_n}{c^2\varepsilon_n^2}
 =\frac{C_0B}{c^2}u_n^{1/3}.
\]
Combining the last four displays,
\[
 \mathbb P_U(\tau_n\notin C_{n,\alpha})
 \le\alpha+2\kappa_n+
 \left(\frac{2z}{\sqrt{2\pi}}+\frac{C_0B}{c^2}\right)u_n^{1/3}.
\]
Both remainder terms tend to zero, proving the claimed conservative lower coverage limit.

For the repeated-star construction of \(\mathrm{def:repeated\text{-}star\text{-}witness}\), direct diagonalization of a star with \(k_n\) leaves gives
\[
 D_n=k_n+1,
 \qquad
 \lambda_n=1+\sqrt{k_n}.
\]
Since \(k_n\sim\beta n^{2/3}\),
\[
 \frac{D_n^2}{n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow\beta^{3/2}.
\]
The nonnormal convergence to \(\mathcal L_\beta\) is exactly \(\mathrm{thm:repeated\text{-}star\text{-}boundary}\).  This verifies the stated elbow illustration, while making no converse claim for arbitrary individual graph sequences.
statements.justification: This corollary converts the proved pointwise graph-sensitive error terms into a directly checkable sufficient rule for normality, feasible studentization, and conservative coverage.
statements.gap: The condition is graph-adaptive and sufficient only; the worst-case maximum-degree theorem, rather than this corollary, carries the necessity claim.
statements.consumer: A future fixed-CGD replication can use the observed graph quantities \(D_n\) and \(\lambda_n\) to verify a less coarse sufficient rule than \(D_n=o(n^{2/3})\).
